name: Rocket Metallic
lede: Rocket Metallic is a muted reddish grey from a web color list, close to several names the ISCC-NBS system filed independently in 1955.

sections.title: A web-list name with ISCC-NBS neighbors
sections.body:
The ColorHub library records Rocket Metallic from Wikipedia's running list of named colors [1]. No book consulted here, and no reliable institutional source found online, confirms who coined the name or why; low-quality color-aggregator sites offer only vague, unsourced guesses, so the origin is left undocumented rather than repeated [1]. The hex #8A7F80 is a screen approximation of a warm, muted grey, close to [[taupe-grey]], about 3.2 units away in LCH space [1].

Several names from the 1955 ISCC-NBS system sit within its block 22: Al Grey, Evenglow, Grey Lilac, Lead Grey and Mist Grey are all near-duplicates of this swatch, though none of them is the name Rocket Metallic itself [1].

Other close matches in the library include [[dark-heliotrope-grey]], [[zircon-grey]] and [[fontainebleau]], read as almost the same or darker than this swatch [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In the ColorHub painting archive this hue appears in 435 of 23,781 paintings, about 1.8 percent, as photographed [2]. It is most common after 1900, and Poul S. Christiansen, Peter Hansen and Fritz Syberg use it far more than the archive average relative to their output [2]. These are computed color matches on varnished, photographed canvases, not pigment identifications [2].
